The data also tags vLLM with open-source and no external data sharing, description of what the product does rather than how well it does it. Beyond the category, the product name, and this short list of tags tied to github.com, the data carries no user counts, revenue, funding, or headcount, so nothing here supports a claim about UC Berkeley / vLLM Team's scale or trajectory.

profile_text.body:
UC Berkeley's vLLM team develops an open-source inference engine for large language models. The project is hosted on GitHub and is self-hosted, meaning users run it on their own infrastructure without external data sharing.

vLLM is categorized as an open source and self-hosted model tool, designed for high-throughput inference. The project appears on the world's most widely adopted developer platform, according to the site's description, where millions of developers and the largest open source community build software.

The vLLM team is based at UC Berkeley, a university research lab, and is a non-profit operation.
